assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's three curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read with its front matter: the canonical OPM_SAITAMA_CHARACTER_STATE_LEDGER.md, read in full (the V01 baseline and every delta through V37, plus the official-web overlay through web287), which the project entrypoint names as its Saitama monograph; and the Saitama rows, transition entries and Saitama-directional relationship entries of the canonical OPM_CHARACTER_MODEL_READINESS_INDEX.md and OPM_RELATIONSHIP_STATE_LEDGER.md. All three cover the Japanese tankobon V01-V37 as canonical and web235-287 as active_provisional. The project method, character modeling schema and CURRENT_STATE_AND_CORPUS_MAP.md were read as method context only. The deep readings, Japanese audits, Checkpoint-A validation ledger and current-release synthesis the items route to are not curated on this row, and no claim rests on them. The project's own 'strong' readiness label is breadth-based and is not adopted. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The Japanese tankobon V01-V37 collected state, with each claim taken at the volume its atom is available from; childhood (V01 extra) and training-year material (V02, V25 extras) are historical states. The active_provisional web overlay is used only for the conduct-first recognition of Amai (web262-263), the Flash boundary (web238) and measurement failure (web248, web277-278), and changes no collected conclusion. No present Saitama action is evidenced after web278.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The dedicated Saitama ledger states conditional rules with their switching conditions and repeated tests across V01-V37: recognition is desired feedback but not the authority for hero action, and Saitama surrenders it when keeping it would devalue other people's meaningful action (V04 ch.22 img 0126; V05 ch.28 img 0149-0155; V07 カツ丼; V08 ch.39 img 0112; V10 suit gift), while the ledger records V15 目撃 as a credit transfer Saitama did not choose and V33 ch.168 as honest attribution rather than costly sacrifice; challenge deprivation is a loss of the uncertainty-effort-learning sequence (V19 Real Punch), activated only by novelty Saitama recognizes as relevant (V10 first Garou contact fails that gate; V11 weak exemplar) and capable of sustained experimental restraint (V13 ch.70-71); immediate physical danger brings intervention, while causes outside his competence bring an admission of limits and low-ceremony availability (V06 鮭; V36 ch.187). Not A: the ledger accretes per-volume deltas rather than one integrated model with fixed priorities, the Checkpoint-A prediction texts and scoring ledger are not curated on this row, and grief appears in one located episode. Not C: the evidence does say which of the competing motives decides the sampled forks (recognition versus others' standing, profit versus rescue at V37 ch.192 img 0136-0139, novelty versus loss at V34 ch.172 img 0026-0028) and predicts Saitama's mistakes, such as projection in the V08 King inference and the V04 collateral blind spot.

Volume-located states from V01 to V37 with an 'available from' boundary on each atom: hobby identity, then registration and the C-class quota (V03), the professional self-description repair to Boros (V06 ch.34 img 0167), King's counsel received but not integrated (V15 to V16), Genos's destruction and the held core (V33 ch.171) with relief and recovered ordinary life (V34), the lost home and room 104 (V35), and the V37 motive correction. Childhood (V01 200円 extra) and training-year states (V02 じぶんみがき; V25 後頭部) are kept as history, not projected forward. V20 and V21 are explicitly recorded as having no diagnostic Saitama behavior. Not A: the grief state is one episode with its aftermath unshown, and the web overlay adds no present action after web278. Not C: the state changes are located at chapter and image level and explained.

The V01 baseline describes plain, direct, colloquial masculine speech with low self-mythologizing, お前 and rougher テメー under irritation, and compressed explanation; the twelve-year-old's polite classroom register (V01 extra 200円 img 0185) shows the adult roughness is contextual. Located switches: roughest register under false public blame (V04 ch.22: うるせぇ, だまれ, テメェら), a plain didactic register while teaching, a plain responsibility register in rescue (V14), an address upgrade to クセーノ博士 once Kuseno becomes concretely salient (V18), and narrow labels such as ただの知り合い (V36 ch.183, ch.187). The ledger adds the control that public speech can be strategically nonliteral (V05 ch.28 img 0151-0154) or compassionately softened (V07 ch.36 img 0111-0113). Not B: systematic voice description stops after V05 apart from scattered quoted lines, the per-volume Japanese dialogue audits the ledger routes to are not curated on this row, and the overlay states that no new voice rule is added. Not D: the forms are tied to recipients and conditions rather than listed.

Ordinary life is unusually well sampled and conditioned: supermarket sales outrank a fight (V02 ch.11 img 0088), real cash scarcity (V05 買えないモノ), the rent-for-cohabitation boundary with Genos (V03 ch.18 img 0068-0069), selling the moon rock (V07), the wallet and cabbage (V18), laundry, free rent in the abandoned district (V25), recurring gaming with King and an 81-0 losing record (V12, V16), hotpot gatherings (V19), pet care for Pochi and rehousing in room 104 (V35), and damaged clothes (V36). The ledger states the rule that extreme combat power does not suppress mundane salience, and marks where it stops: material salience does not outrank rescue ethics (V18; V37 reward return). Not A: private routine is seen mostly through comic vignettes and extras, and solitary interior life is thin. Not C: the recurring ordinary patterns are explained and located across many volumes.

The relationship ledger gives Saitama-directional entries with located transitions for Genos (from tolerated follower to disciple, rent negotiation, core retention at V33, unusable spar feedback at V37), King (from confession to recurring game friendship, conceptual counsel at V15, operational complementarity at V17), Bang, Fubuki (refuses membership without expelling her; the acquaintance label at V36), Garou (asymmetric non-recognition, then conduct-based recognition and refusal to kill at V32 to V34), Sonic, Suiryu, Tatsumaki, Kuseno, Child Emperor, Flash, Manako and the A-Class neighbors. The conditioning rules are explicit: practical salience rather than formal rank governs deference (V18 Kuseno; V25 Flash), and conduct exceeds labels without authorizing friendship or ownership (V36). Not A: grief and long-horizon repair are observed only with Genos, and Saitama's side of many relations is recorded as action rather than stated feeling. Not C: the ledger says why his response differs by relationship and state.

Some private monologue and reflection is located: the Hammerhead counterfactual (V02 ch.14 img 0159), pedagogical insecurity (V03 ch.18 俺がジェノスに教える事なんてなに一つねーのに), 本当の戦いか……覚えてねぇな (V10 ch.53 img 0103), the reflection on gratitude in the training year (V02 extra), and the absence of excitement when facing full-strength opposition after the loss (V34 ch.172 img 0026-0028). The ledger states that grief and anger at V33 are contextual interpretation and that Saitama's self-account (俺なんもしてねぇよ, V31) underdescribes his influence. Not B: most states are inferred from conduct, and the evidence does not let a model state Saitama's private reasoning in novel situations beyond the sampled reflections. Not D: the available interior statements are located and integrated into the conditional rules.

Conflict behavior is conditioned on opponent category, conduct and relationship: surrender ends force (V02 Hammerhead), deliberate stopping blows and apology against human rivals (V02 Sonic), incapacitation rather than lethal force against peer heroes even in anger (V04 Tanktop brothers), protected sparring with Genos (V03), compressed attention to physically trivial threats (V19; V23-V24), legibility-gated engagement (V10 Garou as カツアゲ), sustained restraint to preserve a martial test (V13), adversarial inference (V06 ship exit), planned restraint with Garou at V34, and collateral and property limits (V36 外でやれ). The project's readiness index states that readiness measures conditional behavior, never fighting strength. Not A: almost every physical conflict is one-sided, so behavior under a genuinely equal opponent is not sampled. Not C: the switching conditions are explicit and repeated.

Located ethical positions with conditions: shared boredom does not justify victimization (V06 Boros), protective duty is not authorized by supplication (V07 カツ丼), compensation is refused despite need (V05 extra), self-directed eccentricity is permitted but wrongdoing and involving children are not (V22 Phoenix Man), refusal to kill Garou as a hero and because of a child's request (V34 ch.173 img 0105-0118), and the profit-versus-rescue self-correction (V37 ch.192 img 0136-0139). The recurring rule that limits are admitted outside his competence and immediate rescue follows inside it is tested at V06, V36 and V37. Not A: Saitama's ethics are mostly enacted rather than argued, and dilemmas between competing goods, such as two simultaneous rescues or legal duty against immediate action, are not sampled. Not C: the evidence establishes which value decides the sampled conflicts and why.

Located instances: deadpan jokes during the underground route (V27 ch.137), the scalp-reflection exchange (V29 ch.144), sarcastic praise of Garou (V33 ch.168), the マジシリーズ water counter that collapses prestige (V24), gaming play and competitive frustration with King (V12, V16), and the wig-guarding misread as defense (V13). Not B: much of the comedy is narrative construction around Saitama (timing, scale contrast) rather than a modeled policy for when and how Saitama himself jokes. Not D: the instances are located and the play channel with King is longitudinal.

The curated items cover the Japanese tankobon V01-V37 as a completed sequential reading, propagated volume by volume, with chapter and image locators and childhood, training and extra material. The official-web overlay through web287 is labelled active_provisional, and web285-287 add no present Saitama action. Not A: the series is ongoing; the underlying deep readings, Japanese audits, Checkpoint-A ledger and current-release synthesis are routed to but not curated on this row; and some deltas (V09, V17) give an evidence route without image locators. Not C: coverage of the collected horizon is complete and located.

The ledger records many explicit corrections against tempting readings: Saitama is not globally socially obtuse (V02, V05, V06) but is not socially omniscient either (V08 projection); he is not a confident doctrine-builder (V03); nonliteral speech is not habitual lying (V07); combat supremacy is not universal competence (V08 迷い猫; V15-V16 games); boredom does not mean universally short attention (V13); the V13 disqualification and the V15 credit transfer are not ethical sacrifice; the absence of excitement at V34 is not an absence of engagement; the V37 failed feedback remains a failure; and no friendship, romance or cure is read into Fubuki or Tatsumaki (V36). Not A: Checkpoint-A records no CONTRADICT for Saitama in the curated material, so disconfirmation is shown through corrections rather than failed predictions. Not C: the limitations are affirmative and located.

Every atom carries an 'available from' volume, each delta states that it imports no later material, later claims exposed in the V1 corpus are quarantined (V33), and historical states (childhood, training year) are kept separate from the present. The volume headers make chronology conditions possible at sub-volume level where the ledger locates a change (V33 ch.171 loss; V34 ch.173-174 reunion). Not A: several deltas summarize without image locators, and the web overlay's state is provisional. Not C: chronology is explicit enough to choose a state before predicting.

conditions: Illustrative short lines only, never presented as quotation, in plain colloquial masculine register with compressed explanation; rougher forms only under the sampled irritation, public blame or provocation.
Apply the ledger's controls: public lines may be strategically nonliteral (V05) or compassionately softened (V07); do not treat such a line as Saitama's sincere self-description.

Polite or honorific forms only where the evidence samples them (the childhood classroom register; the クセーノ博士 address upgrade at V18); no catchphrase repetition, no grandiose or mentor-doctrine speech.
No audio, accent or native-speaker validation is implied.
scenario_readiness.note: The located register and its switching conditions constrain short lines in the sampled situations. Not READY: the systematic voice description stops at V05 and the Japanese audits are not curated. Not NOT_READY: the baseline, contrasts and quoted forms are located across volumes.

conditions: Name the state first: before V33, or after V34 with Genos restored; household before or after the V35 move; whether Saitama recognizes the opponent or phenomenon as relevant novelty.

Predict from the stated rules (recognition hierarchy, legibility-gated novelty, admission of limits outside competence, practical-salience deference, restraint toward humans and surrender), including the predicted mistakes and failed feedback.
Give outcomes of physical conflict only where Saitama's surplus is not the question; never invent an equal opponent, a power limit or an origin of the power.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Adult professional-hero Saitama after registration (V03) and within V01-V37, with the state named relative to the V33-V34 loss and recovery and the V35 relocation; childhood and training-year states only as history.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The sampled relationships (Genos, King, Bang, Fubuki, Garou, Tatsumaki, Kuseno, Child Emperor, Flash, Manako, the A-Class neighbors), strangers or civilians in need, and opponents in the sampled categories. Transfer to a comparable new acquaintance is a separate, lower-confidence condition justified only by the practical-salience rule.
setting_constraints: The One Punch Man world with the Hero Association, monsters and Saitama's overwhelming physical surplus intact.

No setting that removes his power, gives him an equal, or requires knowledge of systems he is shown not to understand (the Association's workings at V02, the origins of the Empty Void or the Mirror machine).
No romance, family biography or long-horizon therapeutic outcome.

scenario_readiness.note: The conditional rules transfer to bounded novel situations that keep the sampled variables. Not READY: equal-opponent combat, long-horizon repair and competing-goods dilemmas are unsampled. Not NOT_READY: the rules have been tested prospectively across many volumes, with recorded CONFIRM and PARTIAL outcomes.

conditions: Within the sampled circle and settings: domestic life with Genos, gaming with King, meals with Bang, hotpot gatherings, shopping, money and household matters, pets and neighbors.
Keep the rules that ordinary scarcity and timing activate Saitama strongly but do not outrank rescue, and that deference follows practical salience rather than rank.
A new acquaintance is a lower-confidence transfer; do not upgrade an acquaintance to friendship against the V36 labelling evidence.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary life is richly sampled with explicit salience rules. Not READY: solitary interior life is thin and sampled partners are a fixed circle.

conditions: Restrict prediction to the sampled forms: surrender, restraint toward humans, child involvement, collateral and property, recognition versus others' standing, profit versus rescue, killing a defeated opponent, and problems outside his competence.
Present Saitama's ethics as enacted choices with brief plain justification, not as an articulated moral theory.
Do not resolve unsampled dilemmas (simultaneous rescues, legal duty against immediate action) as if the evidence decided them.
scenario_readiness.note: Located ethical positions and decided forks support bounded prediction. Not READY: competing-goods dilemmas and argued deliberation are unsampled.

No romantic relationship of Saitama's is sampled, and the relationship ledger explicitly rejects reading romance, cure or a Blast replacement into the Saitama-Tatsumaki contact (V36). This bounds use of the evidence; it is not evidence that Saitama is incapable of romance.

conditions: Hero Association work in the sampled forms: registration and rank, quota pressure (V03), routine tasks such as the lost cat (V08), temporary teams under practical leadership (V11), unauthorized direct action (V19-V23), refusal of the Neo Heroes transfer (V37) and cross-institution credit (V07).
Keep the poor fit with rigid assigned-role procedure alongside his acceptance of task-relevant authority.
Do not assume Saitama understands institutional schemes he is shown not to know (the V37 fixed match).
scenario_readiness.note: Hero work is the most heavily sampled domain. Not READY: Saitama never holds command or administrative roles, and he enters institutional crises outside formal deployment.

known_limits.statement: Grief and loss are observed in one located episode (Genos's destruction at V33 and his restoration at V34) whose aftermath is short; there is no generalized grief policy, and the readiness index lists sustained grief as missing.

The consequences of Saitama's advice in complex nonphysical problems are open, and his V37 appraisal of Genos fails relationally (Checkpoint S-A-05 PARTIAL); the web overlay does not repair it or make him a general teacher.

Saitama's social perception is selective: acute when a salient value is threatened (V05, V06) but prone to projection from his own experience (V08 King) and to category-driven misreading (V10 Garou). Reconstructions must reproduce both sides.
Saitama's outward lines may be strategic or compassionate nonliteral speech (V05 crowd, V07 Boros); surface dialogue cannot be read as sincere self-description without context.
The web235-287 overlay is active_provisional; web285-287 add no present Saitama action, and the overlay changes no collected-boundary conclusion.
V20 and V21 supply no diagnostic Saitama behavior; nothing is to be inferred from absence or from later material outside those boundaries.

The Checkpoint-A prediction texts and the validation ledger that scores them are not curated on this row; only the per-volume outcomes recorded in the Saitama ledger and readiness index are available, and the project states that checkpoint confirmation is not independent character evidence.

Saitama's behavior against a genuinely equal opponent, or in a crisis where his physical solution is unavailable at life-or-death stakes, is not sampled; game-domain defeats and social problems are the only tests of that kind.
The per-volume Japanese dialogue and register audits are routed to by the ledger but not curated on this row, so voice claims rest on the ledger's summaries and quoted forms.
Romance, family background and adult life before the hero decision beyond the job-hunting and training-year scenes are not sampled.
